Dengue fever and Chikungunya in Costa Rica 
 Subscribe Sign in Latin America and the Caribbean Dengue fever and Chikungunya in Costa Rica
 Robert Herriman Nov 12, 2026 Share Costa Rica officials report an increase in dengue fever in 2026. The Ministry of Health has counted 6,594 dengue cases so far in 2026, compared with 4,181 at the same point last year, or a 57% increase.
 Alajuela province has the most dengue cases at 2,791, followed by Puntarenas with 981 and San José with 880.
 Concerning chikungunya, 1,049 cases have been recorded this year through mid-October.
 The Chorotega health region, which covers Guanacaste, has 602 chikungunya cases, or 57% of the national total. La Cruz, near the Nicaraguan border, has 389, Carrillo has 90 and Santa Cruz has 64.
